S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
examples: Makes mistakes in homework or tests by misreading questions or skipping important parts.
Frequently omits details or makes typos in work documents or reports.
Repeats mistakes in calculations or numerical work, such as switching signs or getting digits wrong.
Performs tasks incorrectly by missing important details in instructions.

S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
examples: Desk, bag, or room is always messy and remains disorganized.
Unable to prioritize or determine the order of tasks, starting them randomly.
Fails to plan time effectively, frequently missing deadlines or rushing to finish at the last minute.
Feels overwhelmed by how to start multi-step projects and procrastinates.

S006.name: Sustained_Mental_Effort_Avoidance
S006.description: Often avoids, dislikes, or is reluctant to engage in tasks that require sustained mental effort.
examples: Continually procrastinates or is reluctant to start writing long reports or complex homework.
Avoids activities that require long periods of concentration, such as reading books or studying.
Passes off tasks that require complex thinking or planning to others.
Gets annoyed or resists when asked to start a task that requires significant mental effort.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
examples: Easily distracted and stops working due to small noises or movements nearby.
Cannot concentrate because eyes keep wandering to the scenery outside the window or people passing by.
Starts daydreaming or gets sidetracked by sudden thoughts while working or studying.
Loses focus and listens in when hearing side conversations or TV sounds.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
examples: Forgets appointment times or meeting schedules, arriving late or missing them entirely.
Forgets to reply to received calls or messages for days.
Frequently incurs late fees because of missing deadlines for utility bills or credit card payments.
Forgets to take medication or leaves necessary items at home when going out.

S015.name: Excessive_Talking
examples: Talks incessantly and cannot tolerate silence, continuing to chatter.
Continues to talk even when others are bored or try to cut the conversation short.
Talks too much inappropriately for the situation, making people around them uncomfortable.
Monopolizes the conversation and gives almost no chance for others to speak.

patient_info.stressor: Juan’s presentation followed the death of a close friend from his soccer league who had also volunteered with him at community health events, leaving Juan to absorb several organizing roles for memorial events, league logistics, and local outreach. Across the next 1 year and 11 months, the added commitments disrupted the checklist-based systems that had long helped him function, and he increasingly made small planning mistakes, struggled to organize multi-site projects, put off mentally demanding reports, became distracted during meetings, forgot calls and community obligations, and talked excessively when trying to compensate socially. The impairment was moderate: he remained employed and respected, but deadlines slipped, colleagues noticed inconsistencies in his usually reliable operations work, and friends began receiving last-minute apologies for missed plans. Juan ultimately asked his primary care physician for a referral to psychiatry after realizing that spreadsheets and reminders were no longer enough to keep his professional and community responsibilities on track.

S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
S001.manifestation: I’ll send out a clinic staffing schedule or a soccer league email thinking I checked it, and then someone points out I put the wrong date, left off a location, or missed a detail that I would’ve caught before.

S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
S005.manifestation: When I’m juggling work projects, memorial committee stuff, and outreach events, I have notes in three different places and I can’t seem to figure out what needs to happen first, so I end up rushing at the end.

S006.name: Sustained_Mental_Effort_Avoidance
S006.description: Often avoids, dislikes, or is reluctant to engage in tasks that require sustained mental effort.
S006.manifestation: The main reason I’m here is that anything that takes real sitting-down brain work, like monthly reports or planning a multi-site health event, feels like I hit a wall and I keep putting it off even when I know it matters.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
S008.manifestation: In meetings, I’ll be trying to listen to a budget update, but a phone vibrating, people talking in the hall, or even a thought about something I forgot for the league pulls me away and I miss the next few minutes.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
S009.manifestation: I’ve been forgetting to return calls from volunteers, missing small errands for events, and once or twice I’ve had to apologize because a community meeting completely slipped my mind until someone texted me.

S015.name: Excessive_Talking
S015.manifestation: I notice I start talking too much when I’m nervous about having dropped the ball, like I’ll over-explain a scheduling mistake and keep going even after the other person clearly got the point.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: Even in elementary school, my teachers told my parents I was bright but always daydreaming, losing worksheets, and forgetting to turn in homework unless my mother checked my backpack every night.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: I’m still getting by at work and in the community, but people have had to cover gaps for me, deadlines have slipped, and I’ve embarrassed myself with last-minute apologies to coworkers and friends.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on for about 1 year and 11 months, since my friend died and I took on more of the league and outreach responsibilities.
